message.content: Rework what PR 490 (`origin/feat/list-props-by-usage`, head 24438c48; `git fetch origin` first; if blocked use existing refs) lists, because I (the lead) misread the user's meaning of 'use'. Branch `fix/list-main-props`; commit locally; I push onto PR 490's branch. Read /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md (incl. Pre-push gate), docs/adr/0028-relevance-evidence-and-the-checker-scheduler.md (incl. the A2 section PR 490 added), the PR body /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/feat-list-props-by-usage.md and /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/fix-list-props-memory.md (keep its memory wins: peak RSS shadcn ~976 MiB, Chakra ~1,825; do not regress them), crates/core/src/relevance/ (`decide`, `Placement`, `narrow`, `apply`), pipeline/semantic_hook.rs, types/semantic.rs, react_types.rs. THE USER'S EXACT WORDS (the product rule, non-negotiable): 'We want to make sure we're providing everything in the main props even if the story doesn't use them. And anything that the actual Button component uses directly. ... It seems like you understood the use to mean used in the story but that is not what I meant.' And earlier: 'produce the best results, not the overwhelming massive numbers that are not useful to anyone'. THE RULE to implement, in BOTH lanes through the one sink: (1) MAIN PROPS ARE LISTED IN FULL: every member of the component's props type that comes from the component's API sources is a listed row, regardless of any story or call site: the props type's own members, members of project sources (collapse still applies to project sources above 200), and members of dependency sources that are API-sized interfaces (e.g. Chakra `ButtonLoadingProps` (loadingText, spinner), `PolymorphicProps` (as, asChild), `UnstyledProp` (unstyled), `JsxStyleProps` (css), `HtmlProps`, the recipe props variant/size/colorPalette/loading/spinnerPlacement). (2) WHAT THE COMPONENT USES DIRECTLY: a member from ANY source, including DOM/ambient/large ones, is a listed typed row when the component's body reads it, destructures it (including with defaults), or passes it explicitly to a child (the T1/T3 body facts: `BodyFacts.reads`, `elements`/attributes, forwarding), never through a spread onto a DOM tag (a DOM spread is no evidence; a spread onto a component resolves to that component's non-ambient props, T3); an unknown body (`handed_on`) is unknown: it does not promote anything and does not hide anything that rule (1) lists. (3) BIG GENERATED / AMBIENT SOURCES STAY AS LAYER NAMES unless (2) promotes a member: the 286 `@types/react` button attributes, `SystemProperties` (706), Chakra `Conditions` (130 `_active`, `2xl`...). Distinguish generated from API by STRUCTURE and PROVENANCE, never by name lists: ambient by declaring path (existing `Origin`), large by the existing collapse thresholds (more than 30 ambient / 200 other), and a source whose members come from a homomorphic mapped type over `keyof` a large interface (Conditions: PR 490's commit 89275198 gives such a member its key's interface as parent) is generated style-system noise: define that rule precisely, justify it, and test it; if a size-only variant gives the same results on the corpora, prefer the simplest. (4) Story args and call-site frequency are NO LONGER the criterion for the main props: keep them ONLY as an additional promotion for members of the noise sources (a story arg naming a collapsed prop makes it a row so the Control shows the arg; call-site floor evidence stays in `decide` as a secondary promotion; if keeping the call-site floor makes the output harder to explain, drop it and say so: simplest correct design wins; amend ADR 0028 A2 via the adr skill with the exact new rule and why (the owner's clarification)). `htmlAttributes` remains 'which DOM attributes are KNOWN'. `collapseInheritedProps: none` still lists everything. Acceptance, measure and put in the PR note: (a) demo sb-demo Button (/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/oracle-run/sb-demo/src/Button.tsx: `ButtonProps & React.ComponentProps<'button'> & { tone, fresh, size, kind, extra }`, body `<button {...props}/>`) lists ALL of Chakra ButtonProps' non-noise members (loadingText, spinner, asChild, as, unstyled, css, variant, size, colorPalette, loading, spinnerPlacement, recipe, html* ...: enumerate which ones exist in the installed @chakra-ui/react types and show them) plus the five own props and children from args, and NOT the 286/706/130 noise members; show the exact row list before (10 rows) and after, in CLI (`extract --src sb-demo/src --json ...`, decode the interned `props`/`propSets`/`nameLists` with a script kept in scratch under /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/oracle-run/ not the repo) and in Storybook dev mode rows (sb-demo/serve.sh; playwright MCP tools via ToolSearch select:mcp__playwright__browser_navigate,mcp__playwright__browser_evaluate,mcp__playwright__browser_wait_for); (b) a component whose body reads `props.onClick` / destructures `{ className = 'x' }` / passes `onFocus={props.onFocus}` to a child lists those DOM props as rows even from the 286-attribute source, and one that only spreads onto `<button>` lists none of them (new tests, both lanes, model-based: extend relevance_model.rs); (c) the main-props DIFFERENTIAL, this time INCLUDING props inherited from dependencies' API interfaces: for every component on gate-large, chakra-only, Mantine, antd, shadcn and Spectrum, the set of members that sit in sources of at most 30 members (any origin except ambient DOM/React/shared-DOM) plus all members of the props type's own declarations must be a subset of the listed rows; report violations (must be 0) and list the 20 most common names hidden by the noise rule so I can eyeball it; (d) row counts for Button on Chakra demo, Mantine, antd, shadcn new-york and aria, Spectrum, react-aria-components: before/after; the five-corpora medians must not blow up (report them: the user's other goal is no overwhelming counts; Chakra's own repo Button was 147); (e) peak RSS shadcn/Chakra not worse than PR 490's current (976/1,825 MiB) beyond 3%; (f) oracle unchanged on antd and shadcn only (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle --corpus antd --corpus shadcn`, authorised): wrong stays 0 / 1. Pre-push gate: invariants, grammar sweep over the source/provenance forms (interface, intersection, mapped-over-keyof, Pick/Omit, alias, generic instantiation, ComponentProps<'el'>, forwardRef/memo wrappers, factory), mutation proofs, `/code-review medium` awaited on your explicit SHA range with one fix round. Gates: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked` (run `pnpm install --offline --ignore-scripts --frozen-lockfile` first), `just test-checker-lane` (symlink target/release in the worktree to your CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release), `just test-ts`, `just semver`; update the changeset `list-props-by-usage` in the user-focused convention of AGENTS.md to describe the rule in the user's terms (main props in full, plus what the component uses; large generated sources as names in a layer). Own CARGO_TARGET_DIR under /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/, rust 1.99.1 first on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin). Cap 100 tool calls; if you run out, stop at a green commit and list what remains. Update the PR body file /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/feat-list-props-by-usage.md with the new rule and tables (replace obsolete claims: Button 10 rows, the Spectrum SharedDom note unless still true). Final message at most 90 words: SHA, the Button rows after (names), main-props differential violations, RSS, gates exit codes, what remains.

Both take a `@types/react` prop only where the structural answer lists it (`react_prop_listed`), and both ask the checker for exactly those names, whatever `htmlAttributes` says.
- **Provenance, not names.** A placed member is kept with the source the structural answer gives it. A listed prop leaves the listing only when its name and its `parent` both match. It then becomes a name in its source's layer: that layer, else the element layer for an ambient source, else a new layer of that parent.
  - A prop with no known source stays listed, in both lanes.
  - A same-named prop from another source is never hidden.
  - A homomorphic mapped type's member (`{ [K in keyof Conditions]?: V }`) now keeps its key's interface as `parent`, as the checker does. Without this, Chakra's condition props had a source in only one lane.
- **Scope.** Only sources outside the project are narrowed: a dependency's, React's or the DOM's, decided by declaring path. Project sources keep the collapse rule. `collapseInheritedProps: none` narrows nothing: it is the expanded view (`relevance: 'all'`).
- **`decide`.**
  - A member passed at the call-site floor is a typed row even if it is ambient.
  - An ambient member the body only reads is a `used` name.
  - An ambient member with unknown evidence is a layer name.
  - A member put forward that has no typed row is named in `used`.
  - With no evidence at all, the listing is own, picked, overriding, required and defaulted props. A whole DOM source is never listed.
- **Declined key sets.** A `Pick` or `Omit` (in place or behind an alias) whose keys are not a closed set of string literals narrows no non-ambient source (D5). React's and the DOM's attributes are still narrowed. Keys a `Pick` names through `Omit`, `Partial`, `Required`, `Readonly` or a project alias count as picked.

- `relevance::Placement::left` held one `(name, type name, file path)` triple per member left out of the listing, on every component, for the whole run. Most paths are long `node_modules` paths, so on shadcn this cost about 110 MiB in the structural pass.
- `LayerFacts::members`, which every checker target carries, held every layer member as the same kind of triple. This was the "+130 MiB in the component phase" that the profile could not explain.

Both now group names under their source: one `(type name, file)` key per source per component, with the names sorted (`Box<[Box<str>]>`), and lookups use binary search. The placement also drops the project's own sources: `narrow` never moves a prop whose source is in the project, so holding them did nothing. The new representation answers every membership question the old triple sets answered, so the output is unchanged.

Not done, measured as not needed: sharing `InheritedLayer.members` between components (brief item 2). After the two fixes every corpus's peak RSS is at or below main's, so the public type stays as it is and no changeset is needed. `Placement` stays on the entry (brief item 1): the merges of checker props call `narrow` again, so the decision is still needed. It is now small.

Invariants:
- `Placement::leaves(name, parent)` is true exactly when PR 490's `left.contains(&(name, parent.name, parent.file_name))` was true, for every parent outside the project. For a project parent it is now false, where PR 490 could say true. `narrow` keeps a project-origin prop listed either way, because its origin check runs straight after `leaves`.
- `LayerFacts::members`, flattened, is the same set of (name, type, file) triples as before. It holds no source with an empty name list, so `may_layer`'s `is_empty` and the derived `Eq`/`Hash` behave as they did on the set.
- Each grouped source is held once per component, with its names sorted and each name once. `leaves` depends on this ordering for its binary search.

13	### A. Relevance decides what is shown, from evidence
14	
15	The owner's rules: returning all resolved props is useless for Storybook and agents; relevance decides what to show; it is derived from evidence, with no name lists; agent output is narrowed later.
16	
17	**Signals.** Each prop a component's props type reaches gets evidence from four places.
18	
19	- **The props type.** A member the props type declares itself is always shown. So is each key of `Pick<X, 'a' | 'b'>`, named on purpose; `Omit<X, 'k'>` says only that `k` is gone, nothing about the rest. A member that redeclares or narrows a base member is the component's own. A required member is shown (a story cannot render without it), and so is one with a `@default` tag or a destructuring default in the body (the component handles it). JSDoc and a literal-union type do not show a member on their own: as promoters they would list every documented member of a style system; they order the shown rows (open question 1).
20	- **Spreads in the body** (T1's `ComponentMapping::body`). `{...rest}` on a DOM tag passes the ambient DOM attributes: no evidence, ignored. A spread onto a component is one hop to that component's own non-ambient props, with the JSX tag resolved to the component by symbol and import (ADR 0027's identity, never the display name). An attribute set after the spread is fixed and subtracted; one set before it is an overridable default and kept; an attribute whose value is one of the component's own props adds nothing. A name in `reads` is shown when its source is not ambient.
21	- **Call sites.** The props consumers pass at JSX usages across the project (T1's `SourceData::jsx_usages`) and in stories' `args`, counted per component with a floor of `max(2, 20%)` of its sites. The baseline puts the cost at 0.30 (Mantine), 0.03 (Spectrum), 0.76 (shadcn) and 0.24 (antd) extra entries per component.
22	- **Unknown.** When `handed_on` is true, `reads` is incomplete (T1's contract), and the body says nothing: never guessed. The member falls back to today's single collapse decision with the reaching count (`CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` in the collapse PR; on main it is still `ResolutionContext::collapses`, `resolver/mod.rs:595`, by declared count, so `decide` is wired only after that PR merges), so missing evidence never hides more than today.
23	
24	**Ambient** is decided by where a member is declared, not by its name: a member `@types/react` declares (by declaring path, as `is_react_declared` in `crates/semantic/src/component.rs` recognizes React terminals), or one that reaches the component only through a spread onto a DOM tag. Each lane computes the bit for each prop and hands it to `decide` in `Evidence` (`is_react_declared` is private to `caliper-docgen-semantic`, which core does not depend on); `decide` never recomputes it, and a model test in the style of the collapse PR's `collapse_model.rs` holds the two lanes to the same bits. `ambient.rs`'s name clauses and `notable_html_attrs` stay as the unknown-evidence fallback until the T5 gate shows evidence replaces them; then they are deleted (slice R9).
25	
26	**Combination.** One function, `relevance::decide(&Evidence) -> Shown`, owns it, as `CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` owns collapsing; both lanes and every surface call it.
27	
28	- Shown as a row: own, picked, overriding, required, defaulted; a non-ambient member that is forwarded, read, or passed at the floor.
29	- Named in the layer's `used` list: an ambient member passed at the floor or read in the body.
30	- Left in a collapsed layer: everything else with complete evidence, even from a source today's rule lists (its source becomes a layer). A non-ambient member with unknown body evidence and no other signal is listed or collapsed as today.
31	
32	**Output.** A collapsed `InheritedLayer` (`crates/core/src/types/output.rs:83`) gains `used`: the names of its members that evidence put forward, written once as a name list (ADR 0018), not as typed rows. Universal props such as `className`, `style` and `id` cost a name each instead of a row each. A `React.ComponentProps<"el">` layer also gets its `members`, so a reader can check `used` against it. No per-prop flag in this ADR: the row/layer split already says shown or not, and why a row is shown is for the agent output, deferred. `SCHEMA_VERSION` goes from 7 to 8 (ADR 0017), with the RDT view, the JSON schema, `binding.d.ts` and a changeset.
33	
34	**Consumers.** The Storybook addon makes argTypes from rows, then one name-only row per `used` name with the layer as its category; an option (`relevance: 'all'`) asks for the expanded output, which is today's `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'`. CLI JSON and TOON carry the same output. Agent output keeps its current form until the agent flow is narrowed.
35	
36	**Acceptance gate** (T5's metric, ported into the weekly by T4). Coverage counts a passed prop as visible when it is a row or in `used`. Call-site evidence is computed from half of the files (by path hash) and coverage is measured on the other half, so the gate does not pass by construction. On the half the floor is `max(1, 20%)`, and only components with at least 6 sites are measured, so the gate does not test a stricter rule than the one shipped.
37	
38	- Coverage mean rises: shadcn 0.43 to at least 0.70; Mantine 0.86 to at least 0.88; antd 0.91 to at least 0.93; Spectrum stays at least 0.96.
39	- Rows shown fall: the median rows per component does not rise on any corpus (Mantine 77, Spectrum 74, shadcn 3, antd 17), and total rows fall on Mantine and Spectrum. Chakra `Button`'s typed rows stay at or under 146 (its `used` names come on top and are reported apart).
40	- These targets are proposals. Only the extra-entry costs above were measured; the fall in rows is not predicted.
41	
42	### A2. The listing follows the decision (slice T4, amended 2026-11-16)
43	
44	Measured at de016f69 (`caliper-fixtures/oracle-run/diagnosis.md`): Storybook listed 437 Controls rows for a demo Chakra `Button` and 280 for a `ComponentProps<'span'>` `Badge`, because `decide` only wrote `used` lists while `htmlAttributes: 'full'` (ADR 0023) and the session merge (`checker_prop_used`) listed every `@types/react` attribute; the CLI merge dropped them all where a layer existed, so the lanes disagreed (Button 150, Badge 2). Changes to section A:
45	
46	- **One placement, every lane.** `relevance::apply` keeps `decide`'s placement on the entry (`ComponentEntry::relevance`, not serialized) and lists by it (`relevance::narrow`); both checker merges call `narrow` again after laying out the checker's props, and take a `@types/react` prop only where the structural answer lists it (`react_prop_listed`), whatever the mode. A listed prop the placement leaves out moves to its source's layer as a name: the layer of its `parent`, else the element layer for an ambient source, else a new layer of that parent. A prop with no `parent` stays listed, so no name is lost.
47	- **Scope.** Only props a source outside the project declares (a dependency's, React's or the DOM's, by declaring path) are narrowed; the project's own sources keep the collapse rule until a later slice measures them. `collapseInheritedProps: none` narrows nothing: it is the expanded view (`relevance: 'all'`).
48	- **Rows.** A member passed at the call-site floor is a typed row even when ambient (a story needs its control; open question 2). An ambient member the body only reads is a `used` name. A member evidence puts forward that has no typed row (its source is collapsed) is named in `used`.
49	- **Unknown evidence.** An ambient member with unknown body evidence is a name in its layer, not a row: without call sites a component lists its own and declared props, never a whole DOM source. A non-ambient member with unknown evidence is listed as before.
50	- **Provenance, not names.** The placement keeps each left-out member with the source the structural answer gives it (`parent`, or the collapsed layer holding it); a merge narrows a listed prop only when name and source both match, so a same-named prop of another source is never hidden and a member with no structural source is narrowed in neither lane. A homomorphic mapped type's member (`{ [K in keyof Conditions]?: V }`) keeps its key's interface as `parent`, as the checker does.
51	- **Declined key sets.** A `Pick` or `Omit` (in place or behind an alias) whose keys are not a closed set of string literals narrows no non-ambient source: which members reach is unproven (findings D5). Keys a `Pick` names through `Omit`, `Partial`, `Required`, `Readonly` or a project alias are picked.
52	- **JSX children** pass `children` at a call site, after every attribute, as the JSX transform does; layout whitespace and empty expressions pass nothing.
53	- **`htmlAttributes`** (ADR 0023 is cited by `options.rs` but not in `docs/adr`; this amends its contract here) says which DOM attributes are known (as rows or layer names), not how many rows a reader sees; `full` stays the default because a passed attribute can be a typed row only if it is known. `notable_html_attrs` still feeds `curated` mode only; it no longer decides rows under the default, and R9 deletes it.
54	
55	### B. The checker is scheduled by the props that will be shown

- Coverage mean rises: shadcn 0.43 to at least 0.70; Mantine 0.86 to at least 0.88; antd 0.91 to at least 0.93; Spectrum stays at least 0.96.
- Rows shown fall: the median rows per component does not rise on any corpus (Mantine 77, Spectrum 74, shadcn 3, antd 17), and total rows fall on Mantine and Spectrum. Chakra `Button`'s typed rows stay at or under 146 (its `used` names come on top and are reported apart).
- These targets are proposals. Only the extra-entry costs above were measured; the fall in rows is not predicted.

### A2. The listing follows the decision (slice T4, amended 2026-11-16)

Measured at de016f69 (`caliper-fixtures/oracle-run/diagnosis.md`): Storybook listed 437 Controls rows for a demo Chakra `Button` and 280 for a `ComponentProps<'span'>` `Badge`, because `decide` only wrote `used` lists while `htmlAttributes: 'full'` (ADR 0023) and the session merge (`checker_prop_used`) listed every `@types/react` attribute; the CLI merge dropped them all where a layer existed, so the lanes disagreed (Button 150, Badge 2). Changes to section A:

- **One placement, every lane.** `relevance::apply` keeps `decide`'s placement on the entry (`ComponentEntry::relevance`, not serialized) and lists by it (`relevance::narrow`); both checker merges call `narrow` again after laying out the checker's props, and take a `@types/react` prop only where the structural answer lists it (`react_prop_listed`), whatever the mode. A listed prop the placement leaves out moves to its source's layer as a name: the layer of its `parent`, else the element layer for an ambient source, else a new layer of that parent. A prop with no `parent` stays listed, so no name is lost.
- **Scope.** Only props a source outside the project declares (a dependency's, React's or the DOM's, by declaring path) are narrowed; the project's own sources keep the collapse rule until a later slice measures them. `collapseInheritedProps: none` narrows nothing: it is the expanded view (`relevance: 'all'`).
- **Rows.** A member passed at the call-site floor is a typed row even when ambient (a story needs its control; open question 2). An ambient member the body only reads is a `used` name. A member evidence puts forward that has no typed row (its source is collapsed) is named in `used`.
- **Unknown evidence.** An ambient member with unknown body evidence is a name in its layer, not a row: without call sites a component lists its own and declared props, never a whole DOM source. A non-ambient member with unknown evidence is listed as before.
- **Provenance, not names.** The placement keeps each left-out member with the source the structural answer gives it (`parent`, or the collapsed layer holding it); a merge narrows a listed prop only when name and source both match, so a same-named prop of another source is never hidden and a member with no structural source is narrowed in neither lane. A homomorphic mapped type's member (`{ [K in keyof Conditions]?: V }`) keeps its key's interface as `parent`, as the checker does.
- **Declined key sets.** A `Pick` or `Omit` (in place or behind an alias) whose keys are not a closed set of string literals narrows no non-ambient source: which members reach is unproven (findings D5). Keys a `Pick` names through `Omit`, `Partial`, `Required`, `Readonly` or a project alias are picked.
- **JSX children** pass `children` at a call site, after every attribute, as the JSX transform does; layout whitespace and empty expressions pass nothing.
- **`htmlAttributes`** (ADR 0023 is cited by `options.rs` but not in `docs/adr`; this amends its contract here) says which DOM attributes are known (as rows or layer names), not how many rows a reader sees; `full` stays the default because a passed attribute can be a typed row only if it is known. `notable_html_attrs` still feeds `curated` mode only; it no longer decides rows under the default, and R9 deletes it.

### B. The checker is scheduled by the props that will be shown

**Goal:** A future contributor (or you, in six months) understands why a hard-to-reverse architectural decision was made, in under a minute of reading.

## Decide if it's ADR material

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural** — it affects system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format/contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code** — if it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, skip it — it's a commit message, a code comment, or a line in `rdt-coverage.md`, not an ADR. A clever algorithm confined to one function, a naming convention, a behavior-preserving refactor: none of these are architectural even if someone spent real thought on them.

Unsure? Ask rather than guess — writing one nobody wanted is worse than skipping one that mattered.
